Maria (CSM): Quick heads-up — PulseMed goes GA next week. They want explicit SLO acceptance before go-live: uptime 99.9% (monthly) and p95 latency <= 200ms for their tokenized embed endpoints. Also asked how latency credits would be calculated if we miss. Can SRE/SE confirm feasibility and the credit calc? @Sam @Dave
Sam (Solutions Eng): Ok, high-level: we can meet 99.9% and 200ms p95 in the hosted tier with the recommended dedicated plan + prefix caching. Need to lock down test window (30 days) and traffic profile. I drafted an SLO YAML snippet we can drop into the acceptance doc:
```yaml
service: pulsemed-embed
slo:
  - name: uptime
    target: 0.999
    window: 30d
  - name: p95_latency
    target_ms: 200
    percentile: 95
```
Sam (Solutions Eng): For credits, standard ops: credit = min(max(0, (target - observed)/target) * monthly_commit, cap). We should confirm cap with CS.
Dave (SRE): A few infra notes: p95 200ms depends on model size and sequence length. If they use long sequences we'll need batching tweaks and higher qps nodes. Warm-up matters — cold KV cache will spike latency on day 0. Recommend a warm-up run and canary traffic (5% -> 25% -> 100%). Also suggest automatic fallback policy to a lower-latency model variant in case of pressure.
Dave (SRE): Example fallback policy (informal): if p95 > 250ms for 5m AND error_rate < 0.5% -> route to variant-small; emit alert and post-mortem.
Olivia (CS Ops): Noted. I'll capture this in the SLO acceptance packet and add an "operational assumptions" section (warm-up, traffic profile, sequence length). Also adding a checkbox for the canary schedule and a link to runbook.
Olivia (CS Ops): Would love a short note from SE about expected steady-state qps per node (so we can size Dedicated). @Sam can you add rough numbers?
Sam (Solutions Eng): Yes — rough ballpark: 80-120 RPS per A100-equivalent for 512-token sequences with batching; 30-50 RPS for 2k tokens. I'll put conservative numbers in the doc.
Elaine (Enablement): PulseMed asked for a 45m enablement session for their ops and devs focused on SLO reporting and what triggers credits. Can we do this Wed 10am PT? I'll send calendar.
Maria (CSM): Wed 10am PT works for PulseMed. Action items for this thread: 
- [ ] SE: add qps numbers and finalize SLO YAML (Sam)
- [ ] SRE: confirm fallback policy language & warm-up checklist (Dave)
- [ ] CS Ops: assemble SLO acceptance packet and runbook link (Olivia)
- [ ] Enablement: run the 45m session and record (Elaine)
- [ ] CSM: send the acceptance doc to customer and capture signature (Maria)
Sam (Solutions Eng): Draft uploaded: https://redwood-internal.notebooks/slo/pulsemed-draft (internal). Please review before EOD.
deploy-bot: Automated: Canary deploy for pulsemed-embed scheduled for 2024-07-18T18:00Z (job #78912).
Maria (CSM): Great — Olivia, once you add the runbook link I'll send the doc to PulseMed and request signed acceptance. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Olivia (CS Ops): Will do, prepping runbook + evidence checklist now. I’ll post the packet here when ready and attach the warm-up playground instructions.
Dave (SRE): One more note — for credit calc transparency we should include a worked example in the doc with numbers (e.g., target 99.9% -> observed 99.6% -> credit = X). I'll ping finance for the exact monetary conversion factor.
Maria (CSM): Perfect. Follow-ups: tagging this for the renewal review next quarter so we can correlate early reliability signals to renewal risk. Closing thread once packet is sent and session scheduled.
